Riverwalk Augusta GA Guide: The Complete Local's Walkthrough

The Riverwalk Augusta GA is the city's most underrated asset—a 1.5-mile brick-paved promenade along the Savannah River that locals use daily and visitors often miss. This guide covers everything you need to know: where to park, what to see, the best times to go, and where to stay if you want the river experience to last beyond a stroll.

Augusta's riverfront has been transformed over the past three decades. What was once an industrial edge is now a linear park connecting downtown to the Augusta Canal and the city's best outdoor spaces. Whether you're here for a weekend, a Masters Week trip, or a longer stay, the Riverwalk is your starting point.

What Is the Augusta Riverwalk?

The Augusta Riverwalk runs along the Georgia bank of the Savannah River, from the 5th Street Bridge area east to the Augusta Canal headgates and beyond. It's part of the larger Augusta Riverfront and Canal system, and it's free and open to the public daily.

The path is mostly flat, brick-paved, and lined with benches, overlooks, and interpretive signs. It's stroller-friendly, bike-friendly (though bikes are best on the adjacent canal towpath), and popular with joggers, dog walkers, and photographers.

Key Sections of the Riverwalk

  • 5th Street Bridge to 8th Street: The most urban stretch, with views of the bridge and downtown skyline. Close to hotels and restaurants.
  • 8th Street to the Canal Headgates: Quieter, more scenic, with river overlooks and access to the Augusta Canal National Heritage Area.
  • Canal Headgates and Towpath: Where the canal begins. The towpath continues for miles and is a favorite for cyclists and runners.

Top Things to Do on the Riverwalk

Don't just walk it—use it as a base for these activities.

1. Walk or Bike the Path

The full Riverwalk is about 1.5 miles one way, making a 3-mile round trip. Add the canal towpath for a longer ride—it's shaded and flat, following the historic canal that powered Augusta's textile mills.

2. Catch an Event at the Jessye Norman Amphitheater

The amphitheater sits right on the river and hosts concerts, festivals, and community events. Check the city calendar for free summer concerts and the annual Augusta Arts in the Heart festival.

3. Explore the Augusta Canal Discovery Center

At the headgates, the Discovery Center explains how the canal was built in 1845 and why it's still used for hydropower today. It's a small, well-done museum—good for a rainy hour or a history-minded stop.

4. Take a Canal Boat Tour

The Augusta Canal Authority runs guided boat tours on a replica Petersburg boat. It's a relaxing way to learn the history and see wildlife (herons, turtles, sometimes alligators).

5. Photograph the Sunset

The Riverwalk faces west, so sunsets over the Savannah River are genuinely spectacular. The 5th Street Bridge and the overlook near the amphitheater are the best vantage points.

6. Grab a Bite Nearby

Downtown Augusta's dining is a short walk away. Favorites include the Bee's Knees (tapas and sandwiches), Metro Coffee House (a local institution), and the Pizza Joint. For a nicer dinner, try Abel Brown Southern Kitchen or Frog Hollow Tavern.

Where to Park and How to Get There

Parking is the biggest question for first-timers. Here's the breakdown:

  • 5th Street Bridge Parking: There's a lot near the bridge on the Georgia side. It's convenient but can fill up on weekends and during events.
  • Downtown Garages: The city has several garages (e.g., the 7th Street garage) within a short walk of the Riverwalk. Rates are reasonable—usually a few dollars for a few hours.
  • Street Parking: Metered spots exist along Broad Street and side streets. Free after 6 p.m. on weekdays and on Sundays.
  • Augusta Canal Parking: If you're starting at the canal, there's a lot at the Discovery Center (1450 Greene St).

Pro tip: If you're visiting during Masters Week (early April), downtown parking becomes a nightmare. The Riverwalk itself is less crowded, but streets around the 5th Street Bridge are often closed or restricted. Plan accordingly.

Best Times to Visit the Riverwalk

Early morning (7–9 a.m.) is quiet and cool, with the river often glassy. Weekday evenings are also pleasant. Weekends midday can be busy with families and events.

Summer in Augusta is hot and humid—if you're walking midday, bring water and sunscreen. Spring (March–May) and fall (September–November) are ideal. Winter is mild and the Riverwalk is nearly empty.

One local secret: the Riverwalk is at its best during the annual Augusta Arts in the Heart festival in September, when the amphitheater and riverfront come alive with food, music, and art.

Riverwalk Events and Festivals

The Riverwalk hosts several recurring events:

  • Augusta Arts in the Heart: A three-day festival in September with international food, art vendors, and performances.
  • Free summer concerts: At the Jessye Norman Amphitheater, usually on Friday evenings.
  • Fourth of July fireworks: The riverfront is a prime viewing spot.
  • Ironman 70.3 Augusta: The swim portion takes place in the Savannah River, with spectators lining the Riverwalk.

Where to Stay in Augusta (Near the Riverwalk)

If you want more than a day trip, where you stay matters. Downtown Augusta hotels are convenient but come with trade-offs: expensive parking (especially during Masters Week), small rooms, shared amenities, and no direct river access. Generic short-term rentals often mean shared spaces or lackluster outdoor areas.

For a river experience that's genuinely private, consider KJ Augusta Rentals—a 3-acre waterfront property on the Savannah River, just 15 minutes from Augusta National and a short drive from the Riverwalk. Unlike hotels, you get:

  • A saltwater pool overlooking the river
  • 6 kayaks and a private dock with boat slip
  • No shared guests—the entire property is yours (sleeps up to 16)
  • A fire pit, grills, ping pong, cornhole, and a golf tee-off area
  • A private back route to Augusta National that avoids Masters traffic
  • Direct booking—no Airbnb/VRBO platform fees, you pay the owner directly

They offer three stay options: the Entire River House for groups up to 16, the Upstairs River House for smaller groups, and the River Suite for couples. All include access to the waterfront and amenities.

If you're planning a Riverwalk visit, staying on the river extends the experience—you can kayak from the dock, watch the sunset over the water, and avoid the downtown parking hassle. Check availability and book direct at kjaugustarentals.com — no platform fees, you pay the owner directly.

What to Bring and Know Before You Go

  • Comfortable shoes: The brick path is uneven in spots.
  • Water: There are few drinking fountains along the route.
  • Sunscreen and hat: Much of the path is exposed.
  • Camera: The river and bridge views are worth it.
  • Leashed dog: Dogs are welcome on the Riverwalk.

Restrooms are available at the amphitheater and the Discovery Center during operating hours. The path is accessible for wheelchairs and strollers.

Beyond the Riverwalk: Other Augusta Attractions

If you have more time, these are worth adding to your itinerary:

  • Augusta National Golf Club: Home of the Masters (private, but the drive-by is a pilgrimage).
  • Augusta Museum of History: Good overview of the region.
  • Morris Museum of Art: Strong collection of Southern art.
  • Phinizy Swamp Nature Park: Great for birding and easy trails.
  • Broad Street: Downtown's main drag for shops and restaurants.

For kayakers, the Savannah River offers calm stretches near the city—and if you stay at KJ Augusta Rentals, the 6 included kayaks let you launch right from the private dock.

Final Tips for Your Riverwalk Visit

The Riverwalk Augusta GA is a free, accessible, and genuinely enjoyable slice of the city. Go early or at sunset, bring water, and pair it with a canal tour or a downtown meal. And if you want to make the river the centerpiece of your trip, skip the downtown hotel and book a waterfront stay where the river is your backyard.
